80	        # Concurrent mirror writes are serialized by flock (ADR-005) in
81	        # eb_emit_event — flock is the deterministic primitive zbuild requires,
82	        # whereas sqlite3 is optional. The timeout is just a cheap safety net
83	        # for a stale lock holder (#1059 chose 2000ms). The mirror stays in the
84	        # default journal mode: no concurrent reader of events.db exists (jsonl
85	        # is the only read path, via eb_query_events).
86	        _eb_init_err="$(sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 2000" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" <<'SQL' 2>&1
87	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
88	    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
89	    ts TEXT NOT NULL,
90	    run_id TEXT,
91	    issue INTEGER,
92	    type TEXT NOT NULL,
93	    plugin TEXT,
94	    kind TEXT,
95	    payload TEXT,
96	    schema_version INTEGER DEFAULT 1
97	);
98	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_ts ON events(ts);
99	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_type ON events(type);
100	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_run_id ON events(run_id);
101	SQL
102	        )" || { [[ -n "$_eb_init_err" ]] && echo "[event-bus] WARN: sqlite3 failed: $_eb_init_err" >&2; }
103	      fi
104	    fi
105	}

107	# ─── _eb_known_type — schema-as-warn check ──────────────────────────────────
108	# Returns 0 if known, 1 if unknown (but never blocks emission).
109	#

111	# known set now also spans every plugin manifest, so per-emit reading would have
112	# multiplied that fork by plugin count. Composition happens once (per process,
113	# and once per RUN via the file cache in known-types.sh); the check itself is an
114	# associative-array lookup and forks nothing.

117	}

120	# Ported from legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/helpers.sh:431-437; two-pass form mirrors _stage_io_strip_ansi.
121	# LC_ALL=C so sed processes raw bytes without aborting on non-UTF-8 sequences (issue #830).

123	# event, and a sed per call was the single largest exec site in a run (ADR-065).
124	_eb_strip_ansi() {
125	    [[ "$1" == *$'\x1b'* ]] || { printf '%s' "$1"; return 0; }
126	    printf '%s' "$1" | LC_ALL=C sed -E $'s/\x1b\\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z~]//g; s/\x1b.//g'
127	}

129	# ─── eb_emit_event — single source of truth for events ──────────────────────
130	# Usage:
131	#   eb_emit_event <type> [key1=val1] [key2=val2] ...
132	#
133	# Standard envelope fields are picked up from env vars:
134	#   ZBUILD_RUN_ID, ZBUILD_ISSUE, ZBUILD_PLUGIN, ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND
135	eb_emit_event() {
136	    local type="$1"; shift
137	    _eb_init
138	
139	    if ! _eb_known_type "$type"; then
140	        # Schema-as-warn: always log, never block.
141	        echo "[event-bus] WARN: unknown event type '$type' (run_id=${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-})" >&2
142	    fi
143	
144	    # Build payload from key=val args. plugin/kind are also captured here as a
145	    # fallback for the envelope (#1705): emitters outside plugin_hook_call's
146	    # dynamic extent — the contract checker, the tamper check — never see the
147	    # exported ZBUILD_PLUGIN context, and left the envelope's advertised
148	    # .plugin/.kind empty. Captured in this existing loop so the hot path gains
149	    # no subprocess, and applied below only when the exported context is absent.
150	    local _data_plugin="" _data_kind=""
151	    local -a _jq_args=()
152	    local key val
153	    for arg in "$@"; do
154	        key="${arg%%=*}"
155	        val="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${arg#*=}")"
156	        case "$key" in
157	            plugin) _data_plugin="$val" ;;
158	            kind)   _data_kind="$val" ;;
159	        esac
160	        _jq_args+=(--arg "$key" "$val")
161	    done
162	    local payload
163	    if [[ ${#_jq_args[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
164	        payload="{}"
165	    else
166	        payload="$(jq -n '$ARGS.named' "${_jq_args[@]}")"
167	    fi

169	    # ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds
170	    local ts
171	    if _eb_host_is_mac; then
172	        ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z)"
173	    else
174	        ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%3NZ)"
175	    fi

177	    local run_id; run_id="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}")"

179	    local plugin; plugin="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_PLUGIN:-}")"
180	    local kind; kind="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND:-}")"
181	    # Fall back to the payload's own plugin/kind so the envelope is populated
182	    # for every emitter, not only those dispatched through plugin_hook_call.
183	    # Applied before the SQLite insert too, so both stores agree.
184	    if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then plugin="$_data_plugin"; fi
185	    if [[ -z "$kind" ]]; then kind="$_data_kind"; fi
186	    # ADR-004 / ADR-039 §3: stamp the active stage onto the envelope so the
187	    # router's C6 precondition can be scoped PER-STAGE. Parallel-group members
188	    # (parallel-orchestrator.sh) each export ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE inside their
189	    # own subshell, so a sibling member's `plugin.run.start` can no longer
190	    # become the most-recent event that satisfies/clobbers THIS member's
191	    # `redaction.applied` check. Present ONLY when a stage is active — stage-less
192	    # emits (pipeline.start, template load, bootstrap) keep the canonical 8-key

205	    # when it differs from the stage, so every other envelope is unchanged.
206	    local unit="${ZBUILD_UNIT:-}"
207	    [[ "$unit" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+){0,2}$ && "$unit" != "$stage" ]] || unit=""

229	         + (if $stage != "" then {stage: $stage} else {} end)
230	         + (if $seq != "" then {seq: $seq} else {} end)
231	         + (if $unit != "" then {unit: $unit} else {} end)')"

235	        (

248	    # and interpolated unquoted (INTEGER column). Skipped (incl. the flock on
249	    # the dedicated lock) when the mirror is disabled — e.g. ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB=
250	    # /dev/null, whose .lock redirect would otherwise fail the emit (#1153).

262	        # the jsonl lock): flock is the deterministic primitive zbuild requires
263	        # (ADR-005), so concurrent emitters (#1131) never collide on the mirror
264	        # write. NON-BLOCKING (-n): if another emitter holds the lock, SKIP this
265	        # best-effort mirror write rather than wait — the mirror is unread
266	        # (events.jsonl is the only read path) so a dropped row is harmless,
267	        # and never waiting means a high-emit-rate pipeline (parallel members,
268	        # kill-mid-run tests) pays ZERO added latency for the mirror. Separate
269	        # lock ⇒ the mirror can never block the authoritative jsonl append.
270	        if zbuild_has_flock; then
271	            (
272	                flock -n 9 || exit 0
273	                _eb_mirror_insert "$_eb_insert_sql"
274	            ) 9>"${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB}.lock"
275	        else
276	            _eb_mirror_insert "$_eb_insert_sql"
277	        fi
278	    fi
279	
280	    # Fire-and-forget: emit MUST never fail its caller — eb_emit_event is called
281	    # bare under `set -e` throughout the pipeline, so the best-effort mirror's
282	    # rc (or a flock-block rc) must not become this function's rc. Without this
283	    # the trailing mirror block's exit code propagated out and aborted stages
284	    # (build:fail / test:error) when the INSERT returned non-zero (#1153 fix).
285	    return 0
286	}
287	
288	# _eb_mirror_insert — run one best-effort mirror INSERT; warn (never fail) on
289	# sqlite3 error. Caller serializes via flock. busy_timeout via -cmd (no stdout,
290	# unlike PRAGMA busy_timeout=N which echoes the value) is a safety net for a
291	# stale lock holder (#1059 chose the 2000ms window).
292	_eb_mirror_insert() {
293	    local _eb_emit_err
294	    _eb_emit_err="$(sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 2000" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" "$1" 2>&1)" \
295	        || { [[ -n "$_eb_emit_err" ]] && echo "[event-bus] WARN: sqlite3 failed: $_eb_emit_err" >&2; }
296	}
297	
298	# _eb_sql_escape: double single-quotes for SQLite single-quoted string literals.
299	# Single source of truth; used for every string field in the INSERT above.
300	# $'...' ANSI-C quoting avoids the double-quote context issue (#278) where
301	# ${s//\'/\'\'} would produce literal backslash+quote instead of two quotes.
302	_eb_sql_escape() {
303	    printf '%s' "${1//$'\''/$'\'\''}"
304	}
305	
306	# ─── eb_query_events — minimal read API ─────────────────────────────────────
307	# Usage: eb_query_events [type_filter] [limit]
308	eb_query_events() {
309	    local type_filter="${1:-}"
310	    local limit="${2:-100}"
311	    if [[ ! -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
312	        return 0
313	    fi
314	    if [[ -n "$type_filter" ]]; then
315	        jq -c --arg t "$type_filter" 'select(.type == $t)' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" | tail -"$limit"
316	    else
317	        tail -"$limit" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
318	    fi
319	}
320	
321	# ─── Override emit_event from helpers.sh ────────────────────────────────────
322	# The placeholder emit_event in scripts/lib/helpers.sh delegates here when
323	# the event-bus is sourced. Just redefine the function.
324	emit_event() {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  zBuild event-bus — emit_event with dual SQLite + JSONL writers           ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Single-writer JSONL (flock-guarded) + optional SQLite mirror for durability.
# Schema-as-warn: unknown event types log a warning but never block.
# Events from ARCHITECTURE.md §6.
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT_FOR_EVENTS="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/compat.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT_FOR_EVENTS/scripts/lib/compat.sh"
# The known-type set (#1717): engine config + every manifest's provides.events.
# shellcheck source=known-types.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_EVENT_BUS_DIR/known-types.sh"

# ─── Locations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# An engine run (core/pipeline/runner.sh) ALWAYS pins these to its per-run dir
# (runs/<run_id>/, #887). An UNPINNED caller — an ad-hoc/test invocation that
# sources the event-bus directly — must NOT accumulate into the shared
# ${HOME}/.zbuild/state/events.{jsonl,db}: that store grows unbounded across
# ad-hoc invocations and a stale events.jsonl.lock left by a killed run can
# hang a later run's `flock -w` (#run-hygiene). Resolve the defaults coherently:
#   1. Nothing pinned  → ephemeral, process-scoped dir under the DATA ROOT,
#      never the durable shared global default and never ${TMPDIR}. ADR-059 §1
#      makes the path the keying: a reclaimer deletes a `runs/<id>/` or an
#      `issues/<N>/` and the scope follows from where it sits, so a ${TMPDIR}
#      default is outside every reclaimable path by construction — which is why
#      cleanup.sh needed a ZBUILD_TMPDIR_PATTERNS scanner to sweep ~2300 of
#      these (#2004). ADR-023/ADR-059 §1 also reject ${TMPDIR} for durable
#      state: on macOS its entries can vanish mid-run (#1571, #1609/#1611).
#   2. Only JSONL pinned → derive the dir (hence the SQLite mirror + lock) from
#      it, so a pinned jsonl never leaks a mirror/lock back to the global
#      default (the test harness pins only ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL).
# Explicit ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR / _DB always win.
if [[ -z "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR:-}${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL:-}${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB:-}" ]]; then
    # Same precedence as zbuild_layout_data_root (core/state/layout.sh); inlined
    # because the event bus deliberately sources almost nothing.
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="${ZBUILD_DATA_ROOT:-${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-$HOME/.zbuild}}/ephemeral-events/$$"
elif [[ -z "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR:-}" && -n "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL:-}" ]]; then
    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$(dirname "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL")"
fi
ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR:-${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-${HOME}/.zbuild/state}}"
ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL:-${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR}/events.jsonl}"
ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB="${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB:-${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR}/events.db}"
ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="${ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT_FOR_EVENTS}/config/event-schema.json}"

# ─── _eb_mirror_enabled — is the optional SQLite mirror active? ─────────────
# True only when sqlite3 is installed AND a real DB path is configured.
# ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB=/dev/null is the "JSONL only, no mirror" sentinel (parity
# fixtures use it); its `.lock` path is unwritable, so the mirror — including
# the dedicated lock — must be skipped entirely, not just fail-soft (#1153).
_eb_mirror_enabled() {
    [[ "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" != "/dev/null" ]] && command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# _eb_host_is_mac — true when the host OS is macOS, regardless of ZBUILD_PLATFORM.
# Uses $OSTYPE (bash builtin, zero forks) so map work units exporting
# ZBUILD_PLATFORM=linux on a macOS host get the correct date format.
_eb_host_is_mac() { [[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]]; }

# ─── _eb_init — idempotent setup (dir, lockfile, SQLite schema) ─────────────
_eb_init() {
    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
    : > "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL}.lock" 2>/dev/null || true
    # SQLite mirror (optional, best-effort) — set up the dedicated mirror lock
    # (SEPARATE from the jsonl lock, so a slow mirror never blocks the
    # authoritative append, #1153) and schema only when the mirror is enabled.
    if _eb_mirror_enabled; then
        : > "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB}.lock" 2>/dev/null || true
      if [[ ! -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" ]]; then
        local _eb_init_err
        # busy_timeout via -cmd (no stdout echo, unlike PRAGMA busy_timeout=N).
        # Concurrent mirror writes are serialized by flock (ADR-005) in
        # eb_emit_event — flock is the deterministic primitive zbuild requires,
        # whereas sqlite3 is optional. The timeout is just a cheap safety net
        # for a stale lock holder (#1059 chose 2000ms). The mirror stays in the
        # default journal mode: no concurrent reader of events.db exists (jsonl
        # is the only read path, via eb_query_events).
        _eb_init_err="$(sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 2000" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" <<'SQL' 2>&1
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ts TEXT NOT NULL,
    run_id TEXT,
    issue INTEGER,
    type TEXT NOT NULL,
    plugin TEXT,
    kind TEXT,
    payload TEXT,
    schema_version INTEGER DEFAULT 1
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_ts ON events(ts);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_type ON events(type);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_run_id ON events(run_id);
SQL
        )" || { [[ -n "$_eb_init_err" ]] && echo "[event-bus] WARN: sqlite3 failed: $_eb_init_err" >&2; }
      fi
    fi
}

# ─── _eb_known_type — schema-as-warn check ──────────────────────────────────
# Returns 0 if known, 1 if unknown (but never blocks emission).
#
# #1717: this used to fork `jq` against ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA on EVERY emit. The
# known set now also spans every plugin manifest, so per-emit reading would have
# multiplied that fork by plugin count. Composition happens once (per process,
# and once per RUN via the file cache in known-types.sh); the check itself is an
# associative-array lookup and forks nothing.
_eb_known_type() {
    eb_known_types_has "$1"
}

# _eb_strip_ansi — strip CSI + bare-ESC sequences from a string before JSONL emission.
# Ported from legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/helpers.sh:431-437; two-pass form mirrors _stage_io_strip_ansi.
# LC_ALL=C so sed processes raw bytes without aborting on non-UTF-8 sequences (issue #830).
# No ESC byte → nothing to strip, and no fork: this runs for every value of every
# event, and a sed per call was the single largest exec site in a run (ADR-065).
_eb_strip_ansi() {
    [[ "$1" == *$'\x1b'* ]] || { printf '%s' "$1"; return 0; }
    printf '%s' "$1" | LC_ALL=C sed -E $'s/\x1b\\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z~]//g; s/\x1b.//g'
}

# ─── eb_emit_event — single source of truth for events ──────────────────────
# Usage:
#   eb_emit_event <type> [key1=val1] [key2=val2] ...
#
# Standard envelope fields are picked up from env vars:
#   ZBUILD_RUN_ID, ZBUILD_ISSUE, ZBUILD_PLUGIN, ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND
eb_emit_event() {
    local type="$1"; shift
    _eb_init

    if ! _eb_known_type "$type"; then
        # Schema-as-warn: always log, never block.
        echo "[event-bus] WARN: unknown event type '$type' (run_id=${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-})" >&2
    fi

    # Build payload from key=val args. plugin/kind are also captured here as a
    # fallback for the envelope (#1705): emitters outside plugin_hook_call's
    # dynamic extent — the contract checker, the tamper check — never see the
    # exported ZBUILD_PLUGIN context, and left the envelope's advertised
    # .plugin/.kind empty. Captured in this existing loop so the hot path gains
    # no subprocess, and applied below only when the exported context is absent.
    local _data_plugin="" _data_kind=""
    local -a _jq_args=()
    local key val
    for arg in "$@"; do
        key="${arg%%=*}"
        val="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${arg#*=}")"
        case "$key" in
            plugin) _data_plugin="$val" ;;
            kind)   _data_kind="$val" ;;
        esac
        _jq_args+=(--arg "$key" "$val")
    done
    local payload
    if [[ ${#_jq_args[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        payload="{}"
    else
        payload="$(jq -n '$ARGS.named' "${_jq_args[@]}")"
    fi

    # ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds
    local ts
    if _eb_host_is_mac; then
        ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z)"
    else
        ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%3NZ)"
    fi

    local run_id; run_id="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}")"
    local issue="${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}"
    local plugin; plugin="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_PLUGIN:-}")"
    local kind; kind="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND:-}")"
    # Fall back to the payload's own plugin/kind so the envelope is populated
    # for every emitter, not only those dispatched through plugin_hook_call.
    # Applied before the SQLite insert too, so both stores agree.
    if [[ -z "$plugin" ]]; then plugin="$_data_plugin"; fi
    if [[ -z "$kind" ]]; then kind="$_data_kind"; fi
    # ADR-004 / ADR-039 §3: stamp the active stage onto the envelope so the
    # router's C6 precondition can be scoped PER-STAGE. Parallel-group members
    # (parallel-orchestrator.sh) each export ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE inside their
    # own subshell, so a sibling member's `plugin.run.start` can no longer
    # become the most-recent event that satisfies/clobbers THIS member's
    # `redaction.applied` check. Present ONLY when a stage is active — stage-less
    # emits (pipeline.start, template load, bootstrap) keep the canonical 8-key
    # envelope, so C6 falls back to the run-level last-event check for them.
    local stage; stage="$(_eb_strip_ansi "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}")"
    # #2131 (ADR-064): the stage-io seq label (`6.1.3` = runner cardinal ·
    # cycle iteration · member position) rides the envelope by the same rule
    # as `stage` — present only while a label is exported. It was rendered
    # into the banner and persisted nowhere, so the run-status comment had no
    # key to pair a stage's start with its end. Validated, not ANSI-stripped:
    # the label is engine-generated digits and dots, and anything else is an
    # upstream fault that must not become a row key downstream.
    local seq="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_SEQ_LABEL:-}"
    [[ "$seq" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$ ]] || seq=""
    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): a map member's own name rides the envelope only
    # when it differs from the stage, so every other envelope is unchanged.
    local unit="${ZBUILD_UNIT:-}"
    [[ "$unit" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+){0,2}$ && "$unit" != "$stage" ]] || unit=""

    # Validate-or-cast $issue to a non-negative integer. Coming from env, an
    # unsanitized string here would break the SQL INSERT below ($issue is
    # interpolated unquoted because the column is INTEGER).
    if ! [[ "$issue" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        issue=0
    fi

    local event_json
    event_json="$(jq -cn \
        --arg ts "$ts" \
        --arg run_id "$run_id" \
        --argjson issue "$issue" \
        --arg type "$type" \
        --arg plugin "$plugin" \
        --arg kind "$kind" \
        --arg stage "$stage" \
        --arg seq "$seq" \
        --arg unit "$unit" \
        --argjson data "$payload" \
        '{ts: $ts, run_id: $run_id, issue: $issue, type: $type, plugin: $plugin, kind: $kind, data: $data, schema_version: 1}
         + (if $stage != "" then {stage: $stage} else {} end)
         + (if $seq != "" then {seq: $seq} else {} end)
         + (if $unit != "" then {unit: $unit} else {} end)')"

    # Single-writer JSONL via flock
    if zbuild_has_flock; then
        (
            flock -w 5 9 || exit 1
            echo "$event_json" >> "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
        ) 9>"${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL}.lock"
    else
        # Best-effort fallback
        echo "$event_json" >> "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
    fi

    # SQLite mirror (optional, fire-and-forget).
    # Escape every string field — previously only $payload was escaped, so a
    # plugin emitting e.g. ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND="x'); DROP TABLE events;--"
    # could corrupt the event store. $issue is validated as integer above
    # and interpolated unquoted (INTEGER column). Skipped (incl. the flock on
    # the dedicated lock) when the mirror is disabled — e.g. ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB=
    # /dev/null, whose .lock redirect would otherwise fail the emit (#1153).
    if _eb_mirror_enabled; then
        local _ts_esc _rid_esc _type_esc _plugin_esc _kind_esc _payload_esc
        _ts_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$ts")"
        _rid_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$run_id")"
        _type_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$type")"
        _plugin_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$plugin")"
        _kind_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$kind")"
        _payload_esc="$(_eb_sql_escape "$payload")"
        local _eb_insert_sql
        _eb_insert_sql="INSERT INTO events (ts, run_id, issue, type, plugin, kind, payload, schema_version) VALUES ('$_ts_esc', '$_rid_esc', $issue, '$_type_esc', '$_plugin_esc', '$_kind_esc', '$_payload_esc', 1);"
        # Serialize the mirror INSERT with flock on the DEDICATED db lock (NOT
        # the jsonl lock): flock is the deterministic primitive zbuild requires
        # (ADR-005), so concurrent emitters (#1131) never collide on the mirror
        # write. NON-BLOCKING (-n): if another emitter holds the lock, SKIP this
        # best-effort mirror write rather than wait — the mirror is unread
        # (events.jsonl is the only read path) so a dropped row is harmless,
        # and never waiting means a high-emit-rate pipeline (parallel members,
        # kill-mid-run tests) pays ZERO added latency for the mirror. Separate
        # lock ⇒ the mirror can never block the authoritative jsonl append.
        if zbuild_has_flock; then
            (
                flock -n 9 || exit 0
                _eb_mirror_insert "$_eb_insert_sql"
            ) 9>"${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB}.lock"
        else
            _eb_mirror_insert "$_eb_insert_sql"
        fi
    fi

    # Fire-and-forget: emit MUST never fail its caller — eb_emit_event is called
    # bare under `set -e` throughout the pipeline, so the best-effort mirror's
    # rc (or a flock-block rc) must not become this function's rc. Without this
    # the trailing mirror block's exit code propagated out and aborted stages
    # (build:fail / test:error) when the INSERT returned non-zero (#1153 fix).
    return 0
}

# _eb_mirror_insert — run one best-effort mirror INSERT; warn (never fail) on
# sqlite3 error. Caller serializes via flock. busy_timeout via -cmd (no stdout,
# unlike PRAGMA busy_timeout=N which echoes the value) is a safety net for a
# stale lock holder (#1059 chose the 2000ms window).
_eb_mirror_insert() {
    local _eb_emit_err
    _eb_emit_err="$(sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 2000" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB" "$1" 2>&1)" \
        || { [[ -n "$_eb_emit_err" ]] && echo "[event-bus] WARN: sqlite3 failed: $_eb_emit_err" >&2; }
}

# _eb_sql_escape: double single-quotes for SQLite single-quoted string literals.
# Single source of truth; used for every string field in the INSERT above.
# $'...' ANSI-C quoting avoids the double-quote context issue (#278) where
# ${s//\'/\'\'} would produce literal backslash+quote instead of two quotes.
_eb_sql_escape() {
    printf '%s' "${1//$'\''/$'\'\''}"
}

# ─── eb_query_events — minimal read API ─────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: eb_query_events [type_filter] [limit]
eb_query_events() {
    local type_filter="${1:-}"
    local limit="${2:-100}"
    if [[ ! -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$type_filter" ]]; then
        jq -c --arg t "$type_filter" 'select(.type == $t)' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" | tail -"$limit"
    else
        tail -"$limit" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
    fi
}

# ─── Override emit_event from helpers.sh ────────────────────────────────────
# The placeholder emit_event in scripts/lib/helpers.sh delegates here when
# the event-bus is sourced. Just redefine the function.
emit_event() {
    eb_emit_event "$@"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh — one live GitHub issue comment per run
# (#2131, ADR-064; keeper e-1 lifted from legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-github.sh).
#
# A sidecar the runner spawns beside a run and reaps in its EXIT trap. It READS
# events.jsonl (never writes it — it has no path to the event bus at all) and
# keeps a single comment on the run's issue edited in place: header pinned at
# the top, one row per stage dispatch, newest first, bounded under GitHub's
# 65,536-byte limit. Every GitHub failure is logged to status-comment.log and
# ignored: the run never fails because GitHub did.
#
# Source-only library (`rsc_*`) with a `main` when executed:
#   bash run-status-comment.sh --events <jsonl> --state-dir <dir> --parent-pid <pid> [--once]
#
# No `set -e` at top level — sourced into the runner, which owns its options.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_RUN_STATUS_COMMENT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0 2>/dev/null
_ZBUILD_RUN_STATUS_COMMENT_LOADED=1

_RSC_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_RSC_ROOT="$(cd "$_RSC_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=./helpers.sh
[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_HELPERS_LOADED:-}" ]] || source "$_RSC_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=./identity.sh
source "$_RSC_ROOT/scripts/lib/identity.sh"

# Tunables — one place. Tests shrink the intervals; operators rarely touch them.
: "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_MIN_INTERVAL:=5}"    # seconds between PATCHes (coalesce)
: "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_POLL:=1}"            # seconds between events.jsonl checks
: "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT:=30}"     # seconds per gh call
# shellcheck source=./run-status-render.sh
source "$_RSC_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-render.sh"   # rsc_render_body, rsc_outbound_body, the bound, the marker

# ─── rsc_log <state_dir> <msg> — the sidecar's only sink ─────────────────────
rsc_log() {
    local state_dir="$1"; shift
    printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$*" >> "$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# ─── rsc_enabled <state_dir> <repo_root> — every reason NOT to post ─────────
# Logs the first failing gate. The repo-slug gate is what keeps a test's temp
# repository (no github.com origin) from ever reaching GitHub.
rsc_enabled() {
    local state_dir="$1" repo_root="${2:-}"
    local why=""
    if [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]]; then why="ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0"
    elif [[ "${NO_GITHUB:-}" == "true" ]]; then why="NO_GITHUB=true"
    elif ! [[ "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then why="no issue number (goal run)"
    elif ! command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then why="gh not on PATH"
    elif ! gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then why="gh auth status failed"
    elif ! zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then why="origin is not a github.com repository"
    fi
    if [[ -n "$why" ]]; then
        rsc_log "$state_dir" "disabled: $why"
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# ═══ GitHub I/O — advisory: every function here returns 0 ═══════════════════

# ─── rsc_gh <state_dir> <stdout_file> <args...> — gh under a watchdog ───────
# `timeout(1)` is not on macOS; the runner's bg+sleep+kill pattern is. The
# body travels as `-F body=@<file>` — a background job's stdin is /dev/null,
# and a 60 KB comment must never be an argv word. Returns gh's rc (124 on
# timeout) for the caller's LOG, never its exit; stderr is kept in
# _RSC_GH_ERR so a caller can tell a 404 from the rest. `-F`, not `-f`:
# only --field reads `@file`; --raw-field sends the literal string, and the
# first real run posted its own temp path as the comment (#2137).
_RSC_GH_ERR=""
rsc_gh() {
    local state_dir="$1" out="$2"; shift 2
    local err rc=0 pid wd
    _RSC_GH_ERR=""
    err="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-$state_dir}/rsc-gh-err.XXXXXX")" || return 1
    gh "$@" > "$out" 2> "$err" </dev/null &
    pid=$!
    # The watchdog must not inherit a caller's `$(...)` capture pipe: the
    # substitution would then block until the sleep ended, turning every
    # call into a GH_TIMEOUT-long wait.
    # The watchdog leaves a marker when it FIRES; that, plus a non-zero rc,
    # is what a timeout means. Testing "is the watchdog gone" instead raced a
    # gh that finished in the same instant the sleep ended and reported a
    # successful call as a timeout, dropping the comment id it had returned.
    ( sleep "$ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT"; : > "$err.fired"; kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true ) >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
    wd=$!
    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
    kill -TERM "$wd" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$wd" 2>/dev/null || true
    if [[ $rc -ne 0 && -e "$err.fired" ]]; then rc=124; fi
    rm -f "$err.fired"
    _RSC_GH_ERR="$(head -c 400 "$err" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
        local detail="${_RSC_GH_ERR:0:200}"
        [[ $rc -eq 124 ]] && detail="timeout after ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT}s ${detail}"
        rsc_log "$state_dir" "gh $1 $2 rc=$rc ${detail}"
    fi
    rm -f "$err"
    return $rc
}

121	# ─── Master trap — kills children, calls hook, removes auto temp dir ─────────
122	# _HARNESS_SIGNAL: set by dedicated INT/TERM wrappers before calling cleanup,
123	# so _test_harness_cleanup can re-raise and exit 128+signal instead of
124	# returning into the interrupted test body (which would produce bogus failures).
125	# _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP: idempotency guard — prevents double cleanup when both
126	# a signal handler and the EXIT trap would otherwise call the body.
127	_HARNESS_SIGNAL=""
128	_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=0

130	_test_harness_cleanup() {
131	    [[ "${_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
132	    _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=1
133	    _kill_test_children
134	    _test_cleanup_hook
135	    if [[ -n "${AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -d "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]]; then
136	        rm -rf "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR"
137	    fi
138	    # Wave 19-L (#749): rm each named TEST_TEMP_DIR setup_test_env created
139	    # so tests that forgot _test_cleanup_hook / cleanup_test_env stop
140	    # leaking. Path-prefix guard against accidental rm-rf-/: each tracked
141	    # path must live under the source-time tmp-root captured in
142	    # _ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT. Using the CURRENT $TMPDIR would fail when tests
143	    # re-export TMPDIR (Copilot review #751); the source-time root is
144	    # stable for the process lifetime since AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR was created
145	    # there. (mktemp -d always returns an absolute path so the prefix
146	    # check is meaningful.)
147	    local _trk
148	    for _trk in "${_TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
149	        [[ -z "$_trk" ]] && continue
150	        [[ "$_trk" == "$_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT"/* ]] || continue
151	        [[ -d "$_trk" ]] && rm -rf "$_trk" 2>/dev/null || true
152	    done
153	    # Signal-triggered teardown: clear both the signal trap and EXIT so the
154	    # re-raised signal exits with 128+N (143/130) without running EXIT again.
155	    if [[ -n "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL:-}" ]]; then
156	        trap - "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" EXIT
157	        kill -"${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" $$
158	    fi
159	}

161	# Thin wrappers installed for TERM and INT: record the in-flight signal name
162	# then call the shared cleanup body. The cleanup body re-raises at the tail
163	# so the process exits 128+signal instead of returning into the test body.
164	_harness_signal_handler() {
165	    local _sig="$1"
166	    _HARNESS_SIGNAL="$_sig"

179	assert_pass() {
180	    local desc="$1"
181	    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
182	    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
183	    # #600: ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET=1 suppresses per-assertion echoes to keep the
184	    # pipeline test-stage banner compact. Counters still update; assert_fail
185	    # is intentionally NOT gated (failures always surface).
186	    [[ "${ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
187	    echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${RESET} ${desc}"
188	}

190	assert_fail() {
191	    local desc="$1"
192	    local detail="${2:-}"
193	    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
194	    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
195	    FAILURES[${#FAILURES[@]}]="$desc"
196	    echo -e "  ${RED}✗${RESET} ${desc}"
197	    # An `if`, not `[[ … ]] && …` as the last line: with no detail that returned
198	    # 1, and under `set -e` the file stopped at its first failure — every later
199	    # assertion went unmeasured (#2234; 13 SPECs on #1835).
200	    if [[ -n "$detail" ]]; then echo -e "    ${DIM}${detail}${RESET}"; fi
201	    return 0

322	setup_test_env() {
323	    local test_name="${1:-zb-test}"
324	    # Clean up auto-created temp dir and create a named one
325	    [[ -n "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" && -d "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]] && rm -rf "$TEST_TEMP_DIR"
326	    TEST_TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/${test_name}.XXXXXX")

328	    # master trap. Without this, tests that forget to set _test_cleanup_hook
329	    # or call cleanup_test_env leak the named dir. Audit (2026-06-08) found
330	    # 44 of 245 setup_test_env callsites had this gap → 1,261 leaked dirs.
331	    # The master trap (_test_harness_cleanup) reads _TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS
332	    # and rm -rf's each, in addition to AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR.
333	    _TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS+=("$TEST_TEMP_DIR")

341	    export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin:$PATH"
342	    # Unset ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR so any ambient pipeline
343	    # values do not leak into this test process (#1713). stage-io falls back to
344	    # ${HOME}/.zbuild/state (sandboxed above) when both are unset, landing all
345	    # writes in the sandbox. We unset rather than redirect to avoid perturbing
346	    # plan_context_recover_sidecar_reasoning (which uses these vars when set)
347	    # and other callers that manage their own artifact paths after setup.
348	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/home/.zbuild/state"

350	    unset "${_ZB_TEST_ISOLATED_VARS[@]}"

360	    export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0

362	    # Prevent CI-environment leakage into the test subprocess.
363	    # GitHub Actions exports WORKSPACE_BRANCH and (in some workflows) CI_MODE; if
364	    # those leak into stage-level unit tests they silently divert intake into the
365	    # CI-workspace-branch path, breaking branch-creation assertions.
366	    unset WORKSPACE_BRANCH CI_MODE

368	    # Link real jq if available
369	    if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
370	        ln -sf "$(command -v jq)" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/jq"
371	    fi
372	
373	    # Mock timeout — macOS doesn't have GNU coreutils timeout by default
374	    if ! command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
375	        cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/timeout" <<'TIMEOUT_EOF'
376	#!/usr/bin/env bash
377	shift  # skip the timeout duration
378	exec "$@"
379	TIMEOUT_EOF
380	        chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/timeout"
381	    fi
382	
383	    # Sandbox mktemp shim — macOS only (see auto-init comment above for rationale).
384	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp"

386	        printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n_s="%s"\nif [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp "$_s/tmp.XXXXXX"; fi\nif [[ $# -eq 1 && "$1" == "-d" ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp -d "$_s/tmpd.XXXXXX"; fi\nexec /usr/bin/mktemp "$@"\n' \

392	# ─── Reserved test identity (#1921 follow-up) ───────────────────────────────
393	# Tests used real issue numbers as identity fixtures — 25 of the 29 in use were
394	# live issues or PRs, and #42 is still OPEN. A run keyed to one of those writes
395	# fabricated prior work onto that issue's state branch; measured on this repo,
396	# zbuild/state/issue-999 held 68 commits of test payloads and issue-698 held 121.
397	# Now that CI chains and pushes (#1970, #2006), that reaches origin.
398	#
399	# 9_0000000+ is unreachable: this repo is ~2000 issues in. A stray
400	# zbuild/state/issue-9xxxxxxx ref is therefore unmistakably test residue, safe to
401	# reclaim, and can never be confused with someone's work.
402	# The floor of the reserved range. Read by lint-test-identity and the hygiene
403	# test; zb_test_issue composes its ids to always land at or above it.
404	ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR=90000000
405	export ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR
406	
407	# Sequential within a test file: 90000001, 90000002, … Files repeat the same ids,
408	# which is safe because each runs in its own throwaway repo — and if one ever
409	# escapes, the number identifies it instantly.
410	# The counter lives in a FILE, not a shell variable: callers use $(zb_test_issue),
411	# which runs in a subshell, so an in-memory counter would never advance and every
412	# call would return the same id.
413	#
414	# The id is keyed on the PID so two test files running in PARALLEL never mint the
415	# same one. They otherwise all start at 90000001, and the teardown below deletes
416	# refs from the SHARED checkout — so one file's cleanup could delete a ref another
417	# file was still asserting on. The unit tier is parallel by default (#984), and
418	# more cores make that likelier, which is why it showed on Linux CI first.
419	#
420	# Shape: 9 + PID%1000 (3) + seq (4) — always 8 digits, always >= 90000000.
421	zb_test_issue() {
422	    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
423	    local f="$dir/.zb-test-issue-seq"
424	    local n=0
425	    [[ -r "$f" ]] && n="$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || printf '0')"
426	    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || n=0
427	    n=$(( n + 1 ))
428	    printf '%d' "$n" > "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
429	    local id
430	    id="$(printf '9%03d%04d' "$(( $$ % 1000 ))" "$n")"
431	    # Record it, so teardown removes exactly the refs THIS file minted rather
432	    # than every reserved ref it happens to find.
433	    printf '%s\n' "$id" >> "$dir/.zb-test-issue-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
434	    printf '%s' "$id"
435	}

437	# Goal fixtures get the same treatment: the marker makes zbuild/state/goal-<hash>
438	# traceable back to a test even though the hash itself is opaque.
439	#
440	# The hash is RECORDED as it is handed out, exactly as zb_test_issue records ids.
441	# Without that, goal refs had no teardown and no guard — which is precisely how
442	# the leak fixed in this branch survived a full identity sweep unnoticed. The
443	# derivation mirrors zbuild_goal_key: sha256 of the text with all whitespace
444	# stripped, truncated to 12 hex.
445	zb_test_goal() {
446	    local text; text="$(printf '[zb-test] %s' "${1:-fixture}")"
447	    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
448	    local h
449	    h="$(printf '%s' "$text" | tr -d '[:space:]' | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-12)"
450	    printf '%s\n' "$h" >> "$dir/.zb-test-goal-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
451	    printf '%s' "$text"
452	}

454	# A throwaway repo WITH an origin. setup_git_temp_repo builds the working tree;
455	# this adds the bare remote a push needs. Promoted out of persist-stage-test.sh,
456	# where it lived as _mk_repo.
457	zb_test_repo() {

459	    local remote="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name-remote.git"

462	    local real_git; real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || echo /usr/bin/git)"
463	    (
464	        "$real_git" init -q --bare "$remote"
465	        cd "$repo" || exit 1
466	        "$real_git" remote add origin "$remote"

472	# Reserved-range state refs in a repo (default: the real checkout). Used by both
473	# the teardown below and the suite-wide hygiene guard.
474	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # callers live in tests/, which CI's shellcheck step
475	# does not scan (it covers scripts core plugins), so the optional repo argument
476	# looks unpassed from inside this file alone.
477	zb_test_reserved_refs() {
478	    local repo="${1:-${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}}"
479	    # Prefix glob, then a NUMERIC filter — not 'issue-9???????'. That counted
480	    # characters, so it covered 90000000-99999999 only, while lint-test-identity
481	    # and _cleanup_issue_ref_decision both gate on >= 90000000. An id above the
482	    # 8-digit range would have passed both and been invisible here.
483	    local _ref _n
484	    while IFS= read -r _ref; do
485	        [[ -n "$_ref" ]] || continue
486	        _n="${_ref##*/issue-}"
487	        [[ "$_n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
488	        # An explicit if, not `[[ … ]] && printf`: the && form returns non-zero
489	        # when the test is false, and as the last command in the loop body that
490	        # aborts callers running under `set -e`.
491	        if [[ "$_n" -ge "${ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR:-90000000}" ]]; then
492	            printf '%s\n' "$_ref"
493	        fi
494	    done < <(git -C "$repo" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' \
495	        'refs/heads/zbuild/state/issue-9*' 2>/dev/null || true)
496	}

498	cleanup_test_env() {
499	    # Remove state refs THIS FILE minted and may have written into the real
500	    # checkout. Deliberately not "every reserved ref present": the unit tier runs
501	    # in parallel, so deleting another file's in-flight ref would fail its
502	    # assertions. Reserved-range by construction, so a real issue's branch is
503	    # never touched — not even one already contaminated.
504	    local _minted="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}/.zb-test-issue-minted"
505	    if [[ -n "${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -r "$_minted" ]]; then
506	        local _id
507	        while IFS= read -r _id; do
508	            [[ "$_id" =~ ^9[0-9]{7}$ ]] || continue
509	            git -C "${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" update-ref -d \
510	                "refs/heads/zbuild/state/issue-$_id" 2>/dev/null || true
511	        done < "$_minted"
512	    fi
513	    local _gminted="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}/.zb-test-goal-minted"
514	    if [[ -n "${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -r "$_gminted" ]]; then
515	        local _h
516	        while IFS= read -r _h; do
517	            [[ "$_h" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{12}$ ]] || continue
518	            git -C "${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" update-ref -d \
519	                "refs/heads/zbuild/state/goal-$_h" 2>/dev/null || true
520	        done < "$_gminted"
521	    fi
522	
523	    if [[ -n "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" && -d "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]]; then
524	        rm -rf "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
525	    fi
526	    [[ -n "${ORIG_HOME:-}" ]] && export HOME="$ORIG_HOME" || true
527	    [[ -n "${ORIG_PATH:-}" ]] && export PATH="$ORIG_PATH" || true
528	    # Restore ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR to pre-setup values
529	    # (or unset them if they were not set before this test sourced the helpers).
530	    if [[ -n "${ORIG_STATE_DIR_SET:-}" ]]; then
531	        export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$ORIG_STATE_DIR"
532	    else
533	        unset ZBUILD_STATE_DIR
534	    fi

536	        export ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR="$ORIG_ARTIFACT_DIR"
537	    else
538	        unset ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR
539	    fi

584	# Install an envelope-aware mock claude binary on PATH ($TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin).
585	# Branches on argv: when invoked with `--output-format json` (ADR-018 Pattern 1
586	# decision #8, #476), wraps the payload in a {type:result,result:...} envelope
587	# so the router's `.result` extraction finds it. Otherwise emits the payload
588	# as raw text (legacy text-mode callers).
589	#
590	# Usage:
591	#   install_envelope_mock_claude <payload>                        # payload is inline text
592	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --file <payload_file>            # payload comes from a file at call time
593	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --record-argv <path> <payload>   # also record argv to <path>
594	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --record-prompt <path> <payload> # also record `-p <prompt>` to <path>
595	#
596	# Flags may be combined (e.g. --file + --record-argv).
597	install_envelope_mock_claude() {
598	    local payload="" payload_file="" argv_record="" prompt_record=""
599	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
600	        case "$1" in
601	            --file)          payload_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
602	            --record-argv)   argv_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
603	            --record-prompt) prompt_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
604	            *)               payload="$1"; shift ;;
605	        esac
606	    done
607	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
608	    local mock_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/claude"
609	    cat > "$mock_bin" <<MOCK
610	#!/usr/bin/env bash
611	# Auto-generated by install_envelope_mock_claude (#476).
612	if [[ -n "${argv_record:-}" ]]; then
613	    printf '%s\n' "\$@" > "$argv_record"
614	fi
615	envelope_mode=0
616	prompt_text=""
617	while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do
618	    case "\$1" in
619	        --output-format|json) envelope_mode=1; shift ;;
620	        -p) prompt_text="\${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
621	        *)  shift ;;
622	    esac
623	done
624	# The router sends the prompt on stdin (#1849: argv overflowed at 128 KiB).
625	[[ -n "\$prompt_text" ]] || prompt_text="\$(cat)"
626	if [[ -n "${prompt_record:-}" ]]; then
627	    printf '%s' "\$prompt_text" > "$prompt_record"
628	fi
629	if [[ -n "${payload_file:-}" ]]; then
630	    payload="\$(cat "$payload_file")"
631	else
632	    payload=$(printf '%q' "$payload")
633	fi
634	if [[ \$envelope_mode -eq 1 ]]; then
635	    jq -n --arg r "\$payload" '{type:"result",subtype:"success",result:\$r,usage:{input_tokens:0,output_tokens:0},tool_uses:[]}'
636	else
637	    printf '%s\n' "\$payload"
638	fi
639	exit 0
640	MOCK
641	    chmod +x "$mock_bin"
642	}

644	# Install an envelope-aware ERROR mock claude binary on PATH ($TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin).
645	# Mirrors install_envelope_mock_claude but simulates a failed `claude` run that
646	# still prints a JSON result envelope to stdout and exits non-zero — the exact
647	# shape route.sh persists to its diagnostic sidecar
648	# (${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-…/artifacts}/stage-io/<stage>-sync-error.raw-claude-output.json).
649	#
650	# The default envelope simulates the #1052 dogfood failure: the planner burned
651	# all its turns exploring the repo and hit max_turns before emitting plan.json:
652	#   {"type":"result","subtype":"error_max_turns","is_error":true,
653	#    "num_turns":<N>,"result":"<partial reasoning text>",
654	#    "usage":{input_tokens:…,output_tokens:…}}
655	# then `exit 1`.
656	#
657	# Everything is tunable via env vars read AT MOCK-INVOCATION TIME (not install
658	# time), so a test can export a different value just before calling plan_run and
659	# the same installed binary honors it. This lets one installer cover three cases:
660	#   (a) max_turns exhaustion (defaults).
661	#   (b) a non-max_turns crash — set ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE to e.g. "error" and the
662	#       discriminator (subtype != error_max_turns) stays on the
663	#       claude_cli_failed path.
664	#   (c) a max_turns envelope whose .result IS a valid plan.json — set
665	#       ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT to the plan JSON; recovery should salvage it.
666	#
667	# Env vars (all optional):
668	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE    envelope .subtype     (default: error_max_turns)
669	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_NUM_TURNS  envelope .num_turns   (default: 25)
670	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT     envelope .result      (default: a partial-reasoning blurb)
671	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_RC         process exit code     (default: 1)
672	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_IS_ERROR   envelope .is_error    (default: true)
673	#
674	# Usage:
675	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error                       # max_turns defaults
676	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error --record-argv <path>  # also record argv
677	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error --record-prompt <path> # also record -p prompt
678	#
679	# Flags may be combined. Mirrors install_envelope_mock_claude's recording hooks
680	# so resume/dogfood tests can assert the captured prompt across runs.
681	install_envelope_mock_claude_error() {
682	    local argv_record="" prompt_record=""
683	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
684	        case "$1" in
685	            --record-argv)   argv_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
686	            --record-prompt) prompt_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
687	            *)               shift ;;
688	        esac
689	    done
690	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
691	    local mock_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/claude"
692	    cat > "$mock_bin" <<MOCK
693	#!/usr/bin/env bash
694	# Auto-generated by install_envelope_mock_claude_error (#1052).
695	if [[ -n "${argv_record:-}" ]]; then
696	    printf '%s\n' "\$@" > "$argv_record"
697	fi
698	prompt_text=""
699	while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do
700	    case "\$1" in
701	        -p) prompt_text="\${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
702	        *)  shift ;;
703	    esac
704	done
705	# The router sends the prompt on stdin (#1849: argv overflowed at 128 KiB).
706	[[ -n "\$prompt_text" ]] || prompt_text="\$(cat)"
707	if [[ -n "${prompt_record:-}" ]]; then
708	    printf '%s' "\$prompt_text" > "$prompt_record"
709	fi
710	# Tunable envelope fields — read at invocation time so a test can vary the
711	# shape per call without reinstalling the mock.
712	_subtype="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE:-error_max_turns}"
713	_num_turns="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_NUM_TURNS:-25}"
714	_is_error="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_IS_ERROR:-true}"
715	_rc="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_RC:-1}"
716	_result="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT:-Explored core/ and plugins/ but ran out of turns before emitting a complete plan. Partial findings: the change touches the router and the plan plugin.}"
717	jq -n \\
718	    --arg st "\$_subtype" \\
719	    --argjson nt "\$_num_turns" \\
720	    --argjson ie "\$_is_error" \\
721	    --arg r "\$_result" \\
722	    '{type:"result",subtype:\$st,is_error:\$ie,num_turns:\$nt,result:\$r,usage:{input_tokens:0,output_tokens:0},tool_uses:[]}'
723	exit "\$_rc"
724	MOCK
725	    chmod +x "$mock_bin"
726	}

730	# Fail loudly on an unknown platform argument. A typo (e.g. `lniux`) must NOT
731	# silently skip a test forever while still reporting success — that would let CI
732	# mask a test that never runs. Exits non-zero so the mistake surfaces.
733	_require_known_platform() {
734	    case "$1" in
735	        linux|macos) return 0 ;;
736	        *)
737	            echo -e "  ${RED}ERROR${RESET}: unknown platform '$1' (expected: linux|macos)" >&2
738	            exit 2
739	            ;;
740	    esac
741	}

743	skip_unless_platform() {
744	    local required="$1"
745	    _require_known_platform "$required"
746	    local current
747	    current="$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)"
748	    case "$current" in
749	        Darwin) current="macos" ;;
750	        Linux)  current="linux" ;;
751	    esac
752	    [[ "$current" == "$required" ]] && return 0
753	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
754	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: requires '$required', running on '$current'" >&2
755	    print_test_results
756	}

758	skip_on_platform() {
759	    local excluded="$1"
760	    _require_known_platform "$excluded"
761	    local current
762	    current="$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)"
763	    case "$current" in
764	        Darwin) current="macos" ;;
765	        Linux)  current="linux" ;;
766	    esac
767	    [[ "$current" != "$excluded" ]] && return 0
768	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
769	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: excluded on '$excluded'" >&2
770	    print_test_results

773	# Capability gate: SKIP cleanly when the platform is right but a required tool is
774	# absent or lacks a needed feature, so an unexercisable contract is an honest
775	# SKIP instead of a confusing failure. Args: a human-readable label, then a probe
776	# command (+args) run with output suppressed — e.g.
777	#   skip_unless_capable "setsid -w unavailable" setsid -w true
778	#   skip_unless_capable "flock unavailable" command -v flock
779	skip_unless_capable() {
780	    local label="$1"; shift
781	    "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
782	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
783	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: $label" >&2
784	    print_test_results

965	# ── wait_for_event ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
966	# Bounded poll for a grep pattern to appear in an events/state file (#619's
967	# "wait-for-event-content" pattern; reused by #887/#1127/#1149). Replaces the
968	# anti-pattern of a fixed `sleep N` followed by a single-shot read of an
969	# event/state file — that races a slow CI box (the writer may not have flushed
970	# the line yet). This polls the file until the content appears, bounded by a
971	# generous timeout so a genuinely-never-emitted event still fails fast-enough
972	# instead of hanging.
973	#
974	# Usage: wait_for_event <file> <grep_pattern> [max_iters=600] [interval=0.1]
975	#   - <grep_pattern> is a basic-regex passed to `grep -q` (quote JSON fragments,
976	#     e.g. '"pipeline.start"').
977	#   - Default bound: 600 × 0.1s = 60s — generous enough for a loaded shared CI
978	#     runner, short enough to never wedge the suite.
979	# Returns 0 as soon as the pattern is present; 1 if the bound elapses first.
980	# Does NOT assert — callers decide whether a timeout is fatal so the failure
981	# message stays test-specific.
982	wait_for_event() {
983	    local file="$1" pattern="$2" max_iters="${3:-600}" interval="${4:-0.1}" i
984	    for (( i = 0; i < max_iters; i++ )); do
985	        if [[ -f "$file" ]] && grep -q "$pattern" "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
986	            return 0
987	        fi
988	        sleep "$interval"
989	    done
990	    return 1
991	}

993	# ── assert_event_emitted ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
994	# Asserts that an event of the given type appears in the JSONL events log.
995	#
996	# Usage: assert_event_emitted <desc> <events_jsonl_path> <event_type>
997	assert_event_emitted() {
998	    local desc="$1" events_file="$2" event_type="$3"
999	    if [[ ! -f "$events_file" ]]; then
1000	        assert_fail "$desc" "events file not found: $events_file"
1001	        return
1002	    fi
1003	    local found
1004	    if found="$(jq -r --arg t "$event_type" 'select(.type == $t) | .type' "$events_file" 2>/dev/null)"; then
1005	        found="${found%%$'\n'*}"
1006	    else
1007	        found=""
1008	    fi

1010	        assert_pass "$desc"
1011	    else
1012	        assert_fail "$desc" "event '$event_type' not found in $events_file"
1013	    fi

1016	# ─── setup_git_temp_repo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1017	# Creates a real, minimal git repo under $TEST_TEMP_DIR/<name> with one
1018	# initial commit. Returns its absolute path on stdout. Used by integration
1019	# tests that exercise real `git checkout`/`git symbolic-ref` against an
1020	# isolated repo (issue #484).
1021	#
1022	# Usage:
1023	#   repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo myrepo)"
1024	#   (cd "$repo" && some_test)
1025	setup_git_temp_repo() {
1026	    local name="${1:-gitrepo}"
1027	    local repo="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name"
1028	    mkdir -p "$repo" 2>/dev/null || return 1
1029	    (
1030	        # #2103 / ADR-024: the cd MUST be fatal. `set -e` is inert inside this
1031	        # subshell because its status is tested by `|| return 1` below, so a
1032	        # failed cd would otherwise run every git command in the CALLER'S
1033	        # checkout — which is exactly what committed seed.txt into a real
1034	        # worktree and pushed a branch to the real origin on 2026-09-15.
1035	        cd "$repo" || exit 1
1036	        # Use the real git binary (not whatever PATH shim may be present).
1037	        local real_git
1038	        real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || true)"
1039	        # If a shim like the parity-fixture mock is on PATH, fall back to
1040	        # well-known absolute locations.
1041	        if [[ -z "$real_git" ]]; then
1042	            for c in /usr/bin/git /usr/local/bin/git /opt/homebrew/bin/git; do
1043	                [[ -x "$c" ]] && real_git="$c" && break
1044	            done
1045	        fi
1046	        [[ -z "$real_git" ]] && return 1
1047	        "$real_git" init -q -b main 2>/dev/null || "$real_git" init -q
1048	        "$real_git" config user.email "test@zbuild.local"
1049	        "$real_git" config user.name "zbuild-test"
1050	        "$real_git" config commit.gpgsign false
1051	        echo "seed" > seed.txt
1052	        "$real_git" add seed.txt
1053	        "$real_git" commit -q -m "seed"
1054	        # Normalize default branch name to 'main' for predictable tests.
1055	        local cur
1056	        cur="$("$real_git" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
1057	        if [[ "$cur" != "main" ]]; then
1058	            "$real_git" branch -m "$cur" main 2>/dev/null || true
1059	        fi
1060	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1061	    printf '%s\n' "$repo"
1062	}

1064	# ── setup_git_master_origin (#2103) ──────────────────────────────────────────
1065	# A bare origin whose default branch is `master` (not `main`), seeded with one
1066	# commit, plus a working clone of it whose origin/HEAD → origin/master. Prints
1067	# the clone's path; prints nothing and returns 1 on any setup failure. Extracted
1068	# from tests/integration/intake-branch-ahead-count-test.sh, where a failed seed
1069	# clone let the seeding subshell run — and `git push origin HEAD:master` — in
1070	# the caller's checkout against the caller's origin. Every cd here is fatal
1071	# because each subshell's status is tested (see setup_git_temp_repo).
1072	#
1073	# Usage:
1074	#   clone="$(setup_git_master_origin a)" || fail "setup"
1075	setup_git_master_origin() {
1076	    local label="${1:-m}"
1077	    local bare="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bare-${label}.git"
1078	    local work="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/work-${label}"
1079	    local tmp_init="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/init-${label}"
1080	
1081	    git init --bare "$bare" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1082	    git -C "$bare" symbolic-ref HEAD "refs/heads/master" 2>/dev/null || { printf ''; return 1; }
1083	
1084	    # Seed via a throwaway clone. The clone's OWN rc is checked before the
1085	    # subshell so a clone failure never reaches the cd; the cd is fatal anyway.
1086	    git clone "$bare" "$tmp_init" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1087	    (
1088	        cd "$tmp_init" || exit 1
1089	        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
1090	        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
1091	        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
1092	        # Unborn HEAD: -b names the branch regardless of init.defaultBranch.
1093	        git checkout -q -b master 2>/dev/null || git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/master || exit 1
1094	        echo "seed" > seed.txt || exit 1
1095	        git add seed.txt || exit 1
1096	        git commit -q -m "seed" || exit 1
1097	        git push -q origin HEAD:"refs/heads/master" || exit 1
1098	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1099	    rm -rf "$tmp_init"
1100	
1101	    # The bare repo MUST now carry master; a bare `.git` check downstream cannot
1102	    # tell "seeded" from "empty", and an unborn HEAD makes `checkout master` a no-op.
1103	    git -C "$bare" show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/master || { printf ''; return 1; }
1104	
1105	    git clone "$bare" "$work" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1106	    (
1107	        cd "$work" || exit 1
1108	        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
1109	        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
1110	        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
1111	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1112	
1113	    printf '%s\n' "$work"
1114	}
1115	
1116	# ── install_template_overlay (#1270) ─────────────────────────────────────────
1117	# Copy one or more template fixtures into a repo's per-repo override dir
1118	# (<repo>/.zbuild/templates/<id>.yaml), the generic ADR-016 overlay seam. A test
1119	# that then runs the engine with CWD = <repo> resolves the fixture WITHOUT any
1120	# env var and WITHOUT writing into the tracked config/templates/ — the overlay
1121	# lives entirely inside the test's temp repo (reaped by the master EXIT/INT/TERM
1122	# trap). This replaces the #1268 ZBUILD_TEMPLATES_DIR seam (reverted in #1270):
1123	# no ambient env, no global state; hermeticity comes from CWD isolation.
1124	#
1125	# Each fixture is a `.zbuild/templates/` overlay, so it MUST carry `extends: <id>`
1126	# (ADR-016). The shipped base it extends (usually `simple`) is read from the
1127	# engine tree unchanged — only the overlay id needs a fixture.
1128	#
1129	# Usage: install_template_overlay <repo> <id> [<id> ...]
1130	# install_simple_design_continue <repo> — overlay template `simple-design-continue`:
1131	# the shipped simple.yaml with design_verify_cycle set to on_max: continue.
1132	# #2241: simple.yaml's design cycle is on_max: halt (#2176), and the runner now
1133	# honours it. Tests whose subject is the CONTINUE path past an exhausted design
1134	# cycle (#766, #1217) drive this instead — generated from the real template at
1135	# test time, so it never drifts from it.
1136	install_simple_design_continue() {
1137	    local _repo="${1:?install_simple_design_continue: <repo> required}" _src_root
1138	    _src_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
1139	    mkdir -p "$_repo/.zbuild/templates"
1140	    awk '
1141	        /^id: simple$/ { print "id: simple-design-continue"; print "extends: simple"; next }
1142	        # #2271: the design loop is nested in delivery_loop, which is the
1143	        # top-level loop now — both continue past exhaustion in this overlay.
1144	        /^(design_verify_cycle|delivery_loop):/ { in_dvc = 1; print; next }
1145	        in_dvc && /^[a-z_-]+:/ { in_dvc = 0 }
1146	        in_dvc && /^  on_max: halt$/ { print "  on_max: continue"; next }
1147	        { print }
1148	    ' "$_src_root/config/templates/simple.yaml" > "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-design-continue.yaml"
1149	    grep -q '^id: simple-design-continue$' "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-design-continue.yaml" || return 1
1150	    # Committed, as install_template_overlay_committed does: an untracked
1151	    # overlay leaves the tree dirty and intake refuses to start on it.
1152	    local _git; _git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || echo /usr/bin/git)"
1153	    "$_git" -C "$_repo" add .zbuild/templates >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1154	    "$_git" -C "$_repo" commit -q -m "add test template overlay" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1155	}
1156	
1157	install_template_overlay() {
1158	    local _repo="$1"; shift
1159	    # Fail fast on an empty repo arg (e.g. an unset OVERLAY_REPO): otherwise we'd
1160	    # mkdir/cp into /.zbuild/templates and fail later with a confusing error.
1161	    if [[ -z "$_repo" ]]; then
1162	        echo "install_template_overlay: <repo> argument required (got empty)" >&2
1163	        return 1
1164	    fi
1165	    mkdir -p "$_repo/.zbuild/templates"
1166	    # Repo root derived from THIS helper's location (…/scripts/lib → repo root),
1167	    # not the caller's cwd, so it resolves regardless of where the test runs.
1168	    local _hdir _src_root
1169	    _hdir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
1170	    _src_root="$(cd "$_hdir/../.." && pwd)"
1171	    local _id _src
1172	    for _id in "$@"; do
1173	        _src="$_src_root/tests/fixtures/templates/${_id}.yaml"
1174	        if [[ ! -f "$_src" ]]; then
1175	            echo "install_template_overlay: fixture not found: $_src" >&2
1176	            return 1
1177	        fi
1178	        cp "$_src" "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/${_id}.yaml"
1179	    done
1180	}
1181	
1182	# install_template_overlay_committed <repo> <id> [<id> ...]
1183	# Like install_template_overlay, but COMMITS the overlay into the repo's git
1184	# HEAD. Needed when the runner (or a nested runner) rsyncs the repo and runs
1185	# `git checkout HEAD -- . && git clean -fdq`, which would wipe an untracked
1186	# overlay (state-root-isolation section F, SPEC-7).
1187	install_template_overlay_committed() {
1188	    local _repo="$1"
1189	    install_template_overlay "$@" || return 1
1190	    local real_git
1191	    real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || true)"
1192	    if [[ -z "$real_git" ]]; then
1193	        for c in /usr/bin/git /usr/local/bin/git /opt/homebrew/bin/git; do
1194	            [[ -x "$c" ]] && real_git="$c" && break
1195	        done
1196	    fi
1197	    [[ -z "$real_git" ]] && { echo "install_template_overlay_committed: git not found" >&2; return 1; }
1198	    "$real_git" -C "$_repo" add .zbuild/templates >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1199	    "$real_git" -C "$_repo" commit -q -m "add test template overlay" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1200	}
1201	
1202	# ── install_cycle_mock_stages (ADR-021, #512) ─────────────────────────────────
1203	# Generate plugins for a cycle whose per-stage verdict depends on ZBUILD_CYCLE_ITER.
1204	#
1205	# Usage:
1206	#   install_cycle_mock_stages <plugins_root> <cycle_id> <stage_id> <iter1:iter2:...>
1207	#
1208	# Each stage emits the verdict declared at index (iter-1). Trailing iters reuse
1209	# the last declared verdict. The plugin also writes the primary artifact to
1210	# state/artifacts/<stage>/primary.txt so feedback wiring has something to copy.
1211	install_cycle_mock_stages() {
1212	    # shellcheck disable=SC2034
1213	    local plugins_root="$1" cycle_id="$2" stage_id="$3" verdicts="$4"
1214	    local dir="$plugins_root/agent/$stage_id"
1215	    mkdir -p "$dir"
1216	    local fn="${stage_id//-/_}_run"
1217	    cat > "$dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
1218	id: $stage_id
1219	name: Cycle Mock $stage_id
1220	kind: agent
1221	version: 0.0.1
1222	hooks:
1223	  run: $fn
1224	provides:
1225	  artifact_type: primary.txt
1226	outputs:
1227	  - path: $stage_id/primary.txt
1228	requires:
1229	  core:
1230	    - redaction
1231	EOF
1232	    cat > "$dir/plugin.sh" <<PLUGIN
1233	${fn}() {
1234	    local stage_id="\$1" state_file="\$2"
1235	    local iter="\${ZBUILD_CYCLE_ITER:-1}"
1236	    local verdicts="$verdicts"
1237	    local IFS_save="\$IFS"; IFS=':'
1238	    # shellcheck disable=SC2206
1239	    local -a vs=(\$verdicts)
1240	    IFS="\$IFS_save"
1241	    local idx=\$(( iter - 1 ))
1242	    [[ \$idx -ge \${#vs[@]} ]] && idx=\$(( \${#vs[@]} - 1 ))
1243	    local v="\${vs[\$idx]:-pass}"
1244	    local sdir="\${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-\${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-\$HOME/.zbuild/state}}"
1245	    mkdir -p "\$sdir/artifacts/$stage_id"
1246	    printf 'iter=%s verdict=%s\n' "\$iter" "\$v" > "\$sdir/artifacts/$stage_id/primary.txt"
1247	    # Persist verdict where runner_read_stage_verdict can find it. The simplest
1248	    # path: write to state via jq inline (we lack the verdict.sh API surface in
1249	    # this stub). cycle_dispatch_stage reads _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT, so set it
1250	    # via the state file mechanism the orchestrator scrapes.
1251	    export _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="\$v"
1252	    export _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
1253	    [[ "\$v" == "fail" ]] && return 1
1254	    return 0
1255	}
1256	PLUGIN
1257	    printf '%s\n' "$dir"
1258	}
1259	
1260	# Assert no direct anthropic API calls were made (chokepoint enforcement)
1261	mock_anthropic_api() {
1262	  local mock_dir="${ZBUILD_TEST_TMP:-/tmp}/mocks/$$"
1263	  mkdir -p "$mock_dir"
1264	  cat > "$mock_dir/curl" <<'MOCKEOF'
1265	#!/usr/bin/env bash
1266	if grep -q 'anthropic' <<< "$(printf '%s\n' "$@")"; then
1267	  echo "[mock] ERROR: direct anthropic API call detected — must go through core/redaction" >&2
1268	  exit 1
1269	fi
1270	exec /usr/bin/curl "$@"
1271	MOCKEOF
1272	  chmod +x "$mock_dir/curl"
1273	  export PATH="$mock_dir:$PATH"
1274	}
1275	
1276	# ─── zb_expected_run_state_dir <repo_dir> <issue> <goal> <run_id> ────────────
1277	# The state dir a run WILL use, derived from the SAME resolver the writer uses
1278	# (#141, ADR-059 §1) rather than by hardcoding a layout shape.
1279	#
1280	# Six integration tests pinned `<state_root>/runs/<run_id>` as a literal. That
1281	# made them assertions about the SHAPE of the layout rather than about the
1282	# isolation property each was actually written to prove — so the #141 move broke
1283	# all six at once while none of them was testing the thing that moved. Deriving
1284	# the path keeps each test pinned to its own property and lets the layout change
1285	# again without a six-file sweep.
1286	#
1287	# Honours the caller's HOME / ZBUILD_*_ROOT, and runs with cwd = <repo_dir>
1288	# because the repo segment comes from that repo's git remote.
1289	zb_expected_run_state_dir() {
1290	    local repo="${1:-}" issue="${2:-}" goal="${3:-}" rid="${4:-}"
1291	    local root; root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
1292	    (
1293	        cd "$repo" 2>/dev/null || exit 1
1294	        # shellcheck source=../../core/state/layout.sh
1295	        source "$root/core/state/layout.sh" || exit 1
1296	        # shellcheck source=./identity.sh
1297	        source "$root/scripts/lib/identity.sh" || exit 1
1298	        local key=""
1299	        key="$(zbuild_run_key "$issue" "$goal" 2>/dev/null || true)"
1300	        zbuild_layout_run_state_dir "$key" "$rid"
1301	    )
1302	}
